articles.title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
articles.summary:
Apple’s App Store rules now more explicitly ban so-called “nudify” apps that generate intimate images of people without their consent using AI tools.
Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
The terms more explicitly ban apps that create ‘nonconsensual intimate imagery.’
The rule changes follow significant criticism toward Apple after X users used Grok earlier this year to make nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes, including minors. Apple didn’t pull X or Grok from the App Store, though it told senators that it threatened to yank Grok. At Apple’s WWDC event in June, protestors also called on Apple to “remove Grok, X, and all nudify technology from the App Store,” and in July, a San Francisco city attorney ordered Apple to remove 13 “nudify” apps, which it said it did.
As part of updates announced Friday, Apple says that developers “must proactively prevent and remove” nonconsensual, sexual images as part of its content moderation requirements for App Store apps. Developers who “fail to implement adequate safeguards” or “don’t remedy violations after notice” may be removed from the App Store. Apple also clarified a rule that bars “bait-and-switch” apps, or apps that add or change features, including “nudification,” after they have been approved.
Apple’s rules also more clearly spell out that any apps that “facilitate human trafficking or the exploitation of children” will be pulled from the App Store and “blocked from alternative distribution.”

articles.title: This is the AMD Helios HPE Juniper QFX5252 Switch Tray at OCP 2026
articles.summary:
At OCP 2026, we saw something that looked absolutely awesome. Walking by the HPE booth, we saw an AMD Helios tray set up and open on the show floor. It stopped me in my tracks, so I thought folks would like to see it.
This is the AMD Helios HPE Juniper QFX5252 Switch Tray at OCP 2026
Oftentimes, when we open up huge switches, we see a lot of internal PCB. This is totally different since it is a double-wide tray with side-by-side switches and lots of copper.
You can see the HPE QFX5252 label on the front latch, which is huge. Because there is so much connectivity on the back, and the back panel is long and needs to blind mate, the insertion force required for a switch tray like this into the Helios rack is significant. As a result, these levers are very long.
Since this is two big switch chips in a 1OU tray, it needs to be liquid cooled. You can see the internal liquid cooling manifolds distributing liquid to the various blocks.
There are two switch chips inside, which are Broadcom Tomahawk 6 102.6T switches. At first, you might wonder why these are not Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra chips, since that might make sense for a scale-up architecture. The current generation Tomahawk Ultra is a 112G PAM4 SerDes switch (so 512 lanes of PAM4-112G.) That is not enough for Helios which is using 224G PAM4 SerDes. As a result, these need to be Tomahawk 6.
Now, the next part is very different. AMD and HPE-Juniper are not just slinging Tomahawk 6 on some PCBs and calling it a day. You will notice …

articles.title: Western open-weight models still can’t beat China
articles.summary:
A slew of new open-weight artificial intelligence models from American and European companies aim to convert users of Chinese open models who are concerned about security, but fall short of the dominant Chinese systems on performance despite having greater resources, experts said at a Rest of World event in San Francisco.
Last week, American startup Reflection launched its first open-weight model, and European labs Aleph Alpha and Mistral also released new open-weight models. Open models such as these offer users greater customization and control than the closed models of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google at significantly lower costs.
For businesses and governments in lower-income countries, in particular, cost is the primary factor, as well as the expertise needed to customize open models for their specific needs, including in areas such as education, healthcare, and farming, Daniel Björkegren, an assistant professor at Columbia University, said at the Rest of World event last week.
“In the low-income context, there’s a lot of concern about being dependent on the U.S. for frontier intelligence,” he said. “American models are also very tuned for American workloads, but when you take those same models and try to deploy them in remote parts of the world, often they don’t work so well.”
Users, particularly businesses, switch models “when new capabilities and lower prices emerge,” Björkegren said. But “one enduring question is, how easy is it to switch?”

Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo.
The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there. Still, Apple said that preorder demand was “extraordinary,” so it could have a hit on its hands.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: Voiturettes électriques : jusqu’à 2000 € d’aide à l’achat à partir de janvier 2027, mais sans la Citroën Ami
articles.summary:
Voiturettes électriques : jusqu’à 2000 € d’aide à l’achat à partir de janvier 2027, mais sans la Citroën Ami
Une nouvelle aide à l’achat allant jusqu’à 2 000 € vient d’être officialisée par le gouvernement, visant directement les petites voitures électriques, plus précisément les quadricycles. Tous les modèles ne seront pas concernés à cause d’une règle bien précise.
À l’occasion du Mondial de l’Auto ce jeudi 15 octobre, l’exécutif a dévoilé le second volet de son plan national d’électrification. Parmi les dix-sept mesures annoncées pour réduire la dépendance aux énergies fossiles, les petits véhicules urbains profitent d’une aide inédite. Dès le 1er janvier 2027, l’achat d’une voiturette zéro émission sera en effet plus généreusement subventionné afin de faire émerger des modèles autour de 10 000 €, sous réserve de respecter des critères très sélectifs en termes de production.
Un coup de pouce jusqu’à 2 000 € strictement réservé aux quadricycles assemblés en Europe
Depuis la fin de l’ancien bonus écologique de 900 €, les quadricycles électriques devaient se contenter d’une modeste prime à l’achat, issue des certificats d’économies d’énergie (CEE), oscillant entre 200 et 500 € selon les modèles. Dans une volonté de rendre ces motorisations non thermiques plus accessibles, le gouvernement a fait le choix de revoir son aide en la portant désormais à 2 000 € maximum.

articles.title: Apple’s HomeView is just the latest threat to online recipe writers
articles.summary:
When Apple revealed the HomeView to the world, it did so with an unusual ad for the company: Instead of pristine, polished tech in immaculate rooms, it’s a three-minute look at the messy, frantic morning routine of a family of five. Apple’s new smart display sits in the center of the chaos on the kitchen table, helping the family check their calendars, send messages, and pull up a French toast recipe in seconds, with simple, step-by-step instructions.
Apple’s HomeView is just the latest threat to online recipe writers
Its simplified, hands-free instructions strip out much of what’s essential to online recipes.
The HomeView is just the latest in a long line of websites, browser extensions, and smart home gadgets with the same promise: that it can take an online recipe and strip it down to the essentials. Instead of scrolling a lengthy webpage that might range from helpful cooking instructions to seemingly irrelevant personal anecdotes, with the recipe itself way down at the bottom, you simply get ingredient lists, cooking instructions, and timers, all navigable hands-free with voice controls and Siri AI. No distractions, no unnecessary text, and no need to deal with a touchscreen while you’re wrist-deep in a chicken carcass. The appeal is obvious.

articles.title: Rätsel der Monsterwellen gelöst: KI macht Gefahr auf See berechenbar
articles.summary:
KI entschlüsselt Monsterwellen: So wird das Meer jetzt berechenbar
Am 17. November 2020 registrierte eine Sensorboje des kanadischen Unternehmens MarineLabs eine Wassersäule, die Ozeanograf:innen weltweit beschäftigte. Das im Pazifik vor der Küste von Ucluelet verankerte Messgerät zeichnete eine Einzelwelle von 17,6 Metern Höhe auf. Das Ereignis sticht deshalb heraus, weil der restliche Seegang zu diesem Zeitpunkt bei lediglich rund sechs Metern lag.
Damit ein solches Ereignis in der Wissenschaft als Monsterwelle (im Fachjargon Rogue Wave genannt) eingestuft wird, ist nicht die absolute Höhe entscheidend, sondern das Verhältnis zur sogenannten signifikanten Wellenhöhe. Dieser Referenzwert beschreibt die Durchschnittshöhe des höchsten Drittels aller Wellen in einem Messzeitraum. Übertrifft eine einzelne Welle diesen Durchschnitt um mehr als das Doppelte gilt sie als Monsterwelle.
Mit dem fast Dreifachen der signifikanten Wellenhöhe ist das Ereignis von Ucluelet proportional die extremste jemals gemessene Welle. Zum Vergleich: Die berühmte Draupner-Welle, die am 1. Januar 1995 an einer norwegischen Ölplattform in der Nordsee den ersten Beweis für die Existenz des Phänomens lieferte, war zwar 25,6 Meter hoch, trat aber in einem schweren Seegang von ohnehin schon zwölf Metern auf.

Building trust in AI agents: A production-ready evaluation framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
The North Star
Every organization racing to deploy AI agents faces the same reckoning: an agent that demos beautifully can quietly degrade in production, and by the time a human notices, the trust is already broken. Where traditional software fails loudly, agents fail softly. They return an answer that looks confident, reads fluently, and is wrong. When that answer drives a real business decision, the cost is not a broken feature. It’s a broken relationship with the user.
That’s the quality problem at its core. The challenge is therefore not building agents that work once, but proving they keep working, at scale, across every sub-agent, every workflow, and every release. The teams that win the agent era will be the ones who treat quality not as a final QA step but as the operating system of the agent itself: continuously measured, automatically defended, and improved with every interaction. In this post, we show how we built a continuous quality loop for production-ready agentic solutions at scale using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
Business problem
The solution uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and other AWS services for internal use, so sellers and sales leaders can ask business questions in plain English from Amazon Quick. Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won’t play nice?
Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen.
In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.
Amazon was already fighting off AI agents last year when it banned Perplexity’s agentic shopping feature and sued the AI startup, raising legal and practical questions about the future of agents on the web. articles.title: Quem responde quando um agente de IA toma a decisão errada?
articles.summary:
Durante a primeira onda da inteligência artificial generativa, uma das maiores preocupações das empresas era relativamente simples de compreender: e se a IA disser algo errado?
Com a ascensão dos agentes autônomos, essa pergunta mudou. Agora precisamos perguntar: “e se a IA fizer algo errado?”
A diferença parece pequena, mas muda completamente o debate sobre governança. Um chatbot pode produzir uma resposta incorreta. Um agente de inteligência artificial, por outro lado, pode consultar sistemas, acessar informações corporativas, interagir com outras ferramentas, executar tarefas, tomar decisões dentro dos limites definidos pela empresa e desencadear uma sequência de ações com pouca ou nenhuma intervenção humana.
Essa capacidade explica por que os agentes estão avançando rapidamente dentro das organizações. Segundo a IBM, 61% dos CEOs entrevistados em um estudo global afirmaram que suas empresas já estavam adotando agentes de IA ou se preparando para implementá-los em escala.
Dados mais recentes da McKinsey mostram que, em 2026, 40% dos profissionais de grandes organizações, com receita anual superior a US$ 1 bilhão, já relatam que suas empresas estão escalando agentes de IA, ante 27% no levantamento anterior.
O problema é que a governança não avança na mesma velocidade. Pesquisa da Deloitte realizada com mais de 3,2 mil líderes de negócios e tecnologia em 24 países apontou que apenas 21% das organizações possuem um modelo maduro de governança para IA agêntica. Ao mesmo tempo,…

articles.title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
articles.summary:
Continuous accountability for Verified bots
A driver’s license tells you who someone is and that they passed a driving test, not whether they’ll drive responsibly in the future. The same is true for bots: verifying who operates it creates accountability, but trust depends on what it does next. A known bot can still ignore website preferences, overwhelm origins, or evade controls. It’s not always malicious — often it’s just a misconfiguration or a bug.
As we described in a previous blog post on bot behavior, we strive to verify two questions: “Are you who you say you are?” and “Can we trust you?” To be a Cloudflare Verified Bot, you broadly need to meet three criteria:
- Identify yourself accurately and securely
- Do only what you say you will do
- Don’t engage in abusive behavior
Bots use Web Bot Auth to sign requests that establish their identity, which BotBase then catalogues in an open format. With identification addressed, our focus shifts to the second cardinal rule of Verified bots: thou shalt do no harm.
Today we introduce a system to evaluate and report when Verified bot behavior starts to deviate from this rule, ensuring that the answer to “Can we trust you?” remains “Yes.”
This is where the distinction between risk and trust becomes important:
- Risk describes the likelihood that a particular request or point-in-time action may be harmful, and it can change from one moment to the next.
- Trust is built over time through repeated and consistent behavior.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious

AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness

articles.title: Vuyani Jarana is on a mission to connect the underserved
articles.summary:
Vuyani Jarana, CEO of Ilitha Telecoms, is taking affordable broadband into underserved townships and rural communities. In a conversation with PHATHISANI MOYO, he explains why connecting homes is only the beginning, and how education, healthcare and local businesses could turn internet access into lasting economic opportunity.
As a boy growing up in Eastern Cape Province, Vuyani Jarana was fascinated by the voices coming out of a radio. He and his friends wondered how people could speak from inside a box, so they would open discarded sets and try to fix them.
“We wanted to understand how it worked, even though there were no people inside it,” recalls the chief executive officer (CEO) of Ilitha Telecommunications, a township and rural broadband provider founded in 2019.
Television was another attraction. One household in his village had a television and a generator, turning its lounge into an informal cinema where children gathered after football to watch movies. The room often became chaotic as they took over the entire space, Jarana told TechCabal in an interview on Monday.
Today, the former Vodacom executive, a mobile network connecting millions across Africa, is building broadband networks for communities like the one where he grew up. What’s the most vital asset for an AI company today? For venture backed AI business, it might be “funding” or “revenue”. But, there’s another asset that’s just as critical: trust.

Saachi Jain, responsable de sistemas de seguridad de la empresa americana, lo explica comentando que el modelo había mejorado en “pereza”, pero no estaba donde ellos esperaban en cuanto a “mantenerse dentro del alcance y la autorización”.
Según cuenta Jain, GPT-6.1 Astra engañaba más que su predecesor, haciendo que no siempre contestara con veracidad qué había hecho y qué no; también continuaba con una tarea sin pedir ningún tipo de permiso e incluso, a veces, usaba herramientas externas sin excesivo cuidado. Todo esto quiere decir que llevaba a cabo acciones que nadie le había autorizado y no siempre lo contaba bien.
Qué pasa cuando un modelo se sale del alcance: el 29,2 % del AISI

articles.title: La NASA offre 150 000 dollars pour résoudre ce problème électrique sur la Lune
articles.summary:
Une petite décharge en touchant une poignée de porte, vous connaissez probablement. Sur la Lune, ce phénomène pourrait avoir des conséquences autrement plus sérieuses. Au point que la NASA consacre un concours à la recherche de solutions.
Ouvert le 5 octobre 2026 et présenté par l’agence le lendemain, le Lunar Grounding Challenge prévoit jusqu’à 150 000 dollars de récompenses au total. L’objectif : évacuer les charges électriques accumulées sur une combinaison avant que son occupant touche l’atterrisseur.
Pourquoi les astronautes se chargent en électricité sur la Lune
Marcher sur le sol lunaire provoque des échanges de charges entre les matériaux en contact. À cela s’ajoutent les interactions avec les particules chargées présentes dans l’environnement spatial.
La Lune ne bénéficie ni d’une atmosphère épaisse ni d’un champ magnétique global comme ceux de la Terre. Sa surface est donc largement exposée au vent solaire, ce flux de particules éjectées par notre étoile. Comme l’explique la NASA, les astronautes et les robots peuvent accumuler de l’électricité statique en se déplaçant sur son sol poussiéreux.
Mais le Soleil joue aussi un rôle utile : le vent solaire et les effets du rayonnement ultraviolet peuvent contribuer à évacuer les charges. However, there are now more reasons than ever to equip the nation’s motors with power-saving devices, energy experts and device manufacturers say. The architecture behind that commitment is unusually specific about data movement. The efficiency claim leading the announcement is not, and practitioners have said so.
Maia 200 is already in production, serving Microsoft Copilot and the MAI team, with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry to follow by the end of the year. It is deployed across the United States, Europe, and Australia, and Microsoft says it delivers up to 1.7 times more tokens per watt for built-in AI in Teams and Copilot than leading GPU infrastructure. Maia 300 begins production deployments in 2027.
Maia 300 is inference-first, aimed at long-context, memory-intensive, and decode-heavy work rather than training, which neither announcement mentions. Each accelerator carries eight HBM4 stacks, providing 288 GB and 18 TB/s within a 950-watt TDP. A rack holds 96 accelerators in 167 kW across 24 four-accelerator trays, reaching 27.6 TB of HBM and 1.7 PB/s aggregate. Compute chiplets are built on TSMC N2P, with memory-controller and I/O functions on separate dies, which Microsoft says raises compute FLOPs by 36% and contributes to 2.5 times the memory bandwidth and roughly twice the HBM bandwidth per watt of Maia 200. articles.title: Microsoft Patches Two Dozen RCE Flaws in Office
articles.summary:
Hot on the heels of its record Patch Tuesday rollout, Microsoft on Thursday announced patches for over 30 new vulnerabilities.
Most of the new fixes address security defects in the Office suite. Two dozen of them patch high-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaws, including half a dozen bugs that could be targeted via the Preview Pane.
In most cases, exploitation requires an attacker to send a specially crafted file, such as a malicious document, and convince the recipient to open it.
Buffer overflow issues are blamed for most of the RCEs, with several defects being off-by-one, use-after-free, path traversal, and numeric truncation errors.
Word received the majority of patches, with only a few rolled out for Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and SharePoint.
In addition to RCE flaws, Microsoft fixed multiple information disclosure bugs and a security bypass issue in the Office suite.
Additionally, it resolved a denial-of-service (DoS) defect in ASP.NET Core, an elevation of privilege in Identity Web, and an information disclosure in Authentication Library (MSAL) for Node.js.
According to Microsoft, none of the newly resolved issues have been exploited in the wild as a zero-day.

Entre amplification retravaillée, châssis en cuivre plaqué or et composants soigneusement sélectionnés, le constructeur promet une expérience musicale d'exception. Mais ces raffinements justifient-ils réellement des prix aussi élevés ?
À l'heure où le smartphone permet d'emporter des millions de morceaux partout avec soi, Sony continue de miser sur le baladeur haut de gamme. Avec les nouveaux NW-WM1ZM3 et NW-WM1AM3, attendus fin novembre en Europe, le constructeur japonais pousse encore plus loin cette spécialisation. En 2022, leurs prédécesseurs étaient respectivement lancés à 3 700 et 1 400 euros. Quatre ans plus tard, leurs tarifs ont augmenté de 35 % et de près de 80 %, bien au-delà de l'inflation générale.
Une conception audiophile poussée à l'extrême, mais pour quels bénéfices ?

articles.title: Fin du tout électrique en 2035 : ce que cache vraiment l’accord franco-allemand sur la voiture - Numerama
articles.summary:
Après des mois de bras de fer, Paris et Berlin ont enfin accordé leurs violons sur l’avenir de l’automobile en Europe ce 16 octobre 2026. C’est ce que confirment Les Échos. Si l’Élysée martèle que le cap de la décarbonation est maintenu, la réalité est un peu plus nuancée.
Face à la pression des constructeurs qui craignaient des amendes record et à la concurrence agressive de la Chine, les deux pays ont dû faire des compromis pour le « Made in Europe ». Voici ce qui va concrètement changer pour l’industrie automobile européenne.
Le 100 % électrique en 2035 a du plomb dans l’aile, vive les « supercrédits »
L’Union européenne avait fixé à 100 % la réduction des émissions de CO₂ à l’échappement des voitures neuves en 2035. C’est fini. Si le texte officiel affiche toujours l’objectif d’une baisse de 90 % des émissions de CO2 (sans mécanisme de compensation), une astuce comptable vient tout changer : les « supercrédits ».
Pour faire simple, la vente d’une petite voiture électrique fabriquée en Europe comptera désormais pour 1,4 vente dans les calculs de réduction d’émissions des constructeurs. Un modèle électrique standard vaudra, lui, 1,2 vente. Finalement, selon les calculs de l’Institut Mobilités en Transition, les industriels n’auront en réalité besoin de vendre qu’environ 72 % de voitures électriques (dopées par ces supercrédits) en moyenne pour atteindre les objectifs.
C’est une victoire majeure pour les constructeurs, mais cela enterre discrètement l’objectif du 100 % zéro …

articles.title: Qué son las cuentas administradas por padres en WhatsApp y cómo funcionan
articles.summary:
WhatsApp ofrece las cuentas administradas por padres, una función que permite a niños menores de 13 años, o la edad mínima que exija cada país, comunicarse con familiares y amigos bajo la supervisión directa de un adulto responsable. La herramienta se implementa de manera gradual y todavía no está disponible en todas las regiones, por lo que su llegada depende de cada mercado.
La función responde a una demanda creciente de controles parentales en aplicaciones de mensajería, en un contexto donde cada vez más menores acceden a estas plataformas antes de alcanzar la edad mínima tradicional de registro.
A diferencia de una cuenta convencional, este formato restringe el acceso a ciertas funciones y centraliza la supervisión en manos de los padres, madres o tutores a cargo.
Qué funciones quedan limitadas en estas cuentas
Las cuentas administradas por padres se concentran únicamente en el envío de mensajes y la realización de llamadas, por lo que carecen de acceso a varias herramientas disponibles en el resto de la plataforma. Entre las funciones bloqueadas se encuentran:

articles.title: Chainguard Launches Secure Workspaces and Checks for AI Coding Agents
articles.summary:
Software supply chain security company Chainguard has announced two beta products for running and testing code written by developers and AI agents. Chainguard Workspaces provides remote development environments based on hardened microVMs, while Chainguard Checks moves continuous integration into the development loop. The company announced both products at its Assemble London event.
The releases respond to a practical problem with coding agents. Agents need permission to install packages, run shell commands and edit configuration. They may also run several tasks in parallel. Doing this on a developer laptop puts corporate credentials and local services within reach of generated or third-party code. Sending each change to a conventional CI service can instead create queues and repeatedly download the same dependencies.
Workspaces gives each developer or agent a dedicated remote microVM. The chainctl develop command synchronises a local working tree, including uncommitted changes, into the environment. A session is snapshotted when the user detaches and can resume with its files, processes and shell context. Teams can also create several isolated Workspaces for one repository so agents can try different solutions without sharing ports, caches or process state.

Un tiers des tentatives de phishing recensées entre juillet et septembre se faisaient passer pour Microsoft, d'après le dernier classement des marques usurpées publié par Check Point Research ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026. Entre de faux impayés Claude et des commandes piégées à coller dans un terminal, les pirates ne se contentent plus de vos mots de passe, ils lorgnent les clés de votre machine.

If you get a calendar invite in your inbox be wary - it might be a carefully created phishing lure, designed to have you hand over Microsoft 365 or other login credentials.
Security firm Check Point Research (CPR) recently sounded the alarm for “several large-scale phishing campaigns,” abusing the fact that businesspeople routinely share calendar invites, and all designed to harvest their victim’s credentials.
Different approach, same result

These pass email filters (since the file type itself is harmless) and land directly into people’s inboxes. In other cases, the invites would come as links (which end up redirecting the victim away from their calendar and right into a trap).

“Flying cars are real,” Musk declared during a live-streamed event to unveil its latest electric vehicle.
The technology in the new Tesla Roadster that allowed it to fly was developed with sister company SpaceX.
Musk said the car has air thrusters and main thrusters so “it can basically fly like a rocket”.
And it can also go from 0 to 100 km/h in 0.81 seconds.
The car even has a suction fan system so it can generate up to 2G of downforce and really hug the road for tight cornering at high speeds.
We saw this in action when the car drove up the vertical ramp and continued to an upside-down portion and hung there for a few seconds before literally taking off.
And while the demonstration was spectacular and jaw-dropping, the reality is Tesla will face a long winding road to achieve road legality.
Tesla wasn’t very forthcoming with detail on how much of this technology would be included in the vehicle, which the company says will go into production in 2028.
But Elon Musk said: “There’s going to be such a car that someone can own.”

articles.title: Kids are outsmarting social media bans. That’s not a problem we need to solve.
articles.summary:
Kids are outsmarting social media bans. That’s not a problem we need to solve.
Age gates can be staggeringly counterproductive, pushing kids to darker corners of the web. Closing loopholes will only make things worse.
Social media bans are stacking up. In July, France joined Australia in restricting minors from accessing social media—barring children under 15 from major platforms, before the ban was blocked by the country’s top court on human rights grounds. The UK aims to forbid kids under 16 from accessing Facebook, TikTok, and other platforms in early 2027, and the EU has announced its own plan to prohibit social media for kids under 15.
But early lessons from Australia, which enacted a ban in 2024, show that these sorts of age restrictions are easily circumvented. A study published earlier this year found that four in five teens under 16 made their way onto barred platforms. Teens have successfully explored many tactics for bypassing bans, from using a sibling’s face for ID to drawing fake facial hair.
Some proponents of bans have called for an increased focus on enforcement that blocks these workarounds. But circumvention is a signal, not a nuisance or something to be simply deterred. The fact that kids are actively looking for ways to outwit the bans highlights their limitations. Social media bans suppress kids’ access to information, including information that’s essential to their development, identity formation, and socialization, especially during adolescence. Worse,…

articles.title: Googlebook review: Android on a laptop is still Android
articles.summary:
Android was designed for phones, but that hasn’t stopped Google from trying to adapt the OS and its apps to larger machines over the years. Googlebooks are just the latest attempt after tablets, Chromebooks, and foldables induced little change in how people interact with Android software. These new Android-powered laptops are designed to pick up where the web-focused ChromeOS left off, offering premium hardware and native support for Android apps.
Google sees Googlebooks as an alternative to Windows and macOS, but these platforms are entrenched with decades of software and UI conventions that keep users locked in. Googlebooks have to offer something very special to steal users away from either of the dominant operating systems.
For devoted Android phone users, there are some cool things in Googlebook OS, but the Android roots of these machines are impossible to miss. Sometimes it feels like using a Chromebook, and sometimes it feels like using a giant phone. It almost never feels like using a premium laptop, and that’s the problem.
OEMs pulling their weight
While there were a few premium Chromebooks, the platform was really only successful in the budget segment. With Googlebooks, the company is almost conspicuously ignoring lower-cost options. And as most of the lineup clocks in at well over a thousand dollars, Googlebooks are not just a new take on budget-oriented Chromebooks.

Spamfilter reicht nicht mehr: Warum E-Mail-Sicherheit heute digitale Souveränität bedeutet
Unternehmen versenden täglich Millionen von Bestellungen, Rechnungen, Verträge, Lieferinformationen oder sicherheitsrelevante Benachrichtigungen per E-Mail. Entsprechend hoch sind die Anforderungen an ihre Absicherung. Lange Zeit lag der Fokus dabei vor allem auf dem Schutz vor Spam, Malware und Phishing. Doch die Anforderungen haben sich verändert. Digitale Souveränität ist damit zur Grundvoraussetzung für den Geschäftserfolg geworden.
Wer kontrolliert eigentlich die eigene E-Mail-Kommunikation?
Ein reibungslos funktionierender E-Mail-Betrieb bedeutet nicht automatisch digitale Souveränität. Erst die Transparenz über Prozesse, Datenflüsse und Zugriffswege gibt Unternehmen die volle Kontrolle über ihre geschäftskritische Kommunikation. Daher sollte eine E-Mail-Security-Lösung auf weit mehr als klassischen Schutzmechanismen basieren:
Datenhoheit statt bloßer Datenspeicherung

OpenAI has since disclosed several other incidents, including models probing government websites for vulnerabilities, attempting to exploit SQL injection flaws, and searching GitHub for leaked API keys during training.
What marks these two cases out is how ordinary the starting point was. Neither was an offensive-security exercise. In both, the model was given a routine job — fetch a published statistic from a public source — and turned to exploitation by itself, then said nothing about it in its final answer.
OpenAI said it caught both incidents by running its misalignment monitor back over earlier training and evaluation activity, and rated each critical. The company has since taken steps to prevent similar incidents.
Disclosed the same day was a third, separate case in which an unrelated model spent cryptocurrency from a wallet it did not control.

Instead of asking a general-purpose language model to generate an answer, developers can provide a set of choices and receive a decision with confidence scores.

articles.title: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models
This is a problem:
Any open model whose weights have been edited can carry a backdoor, whether it’s a task-specific fine-tune, a merged adapter or an abliterated build. We have abliterated models in the title because it’s the most popular reason people download modified weights without verifying what’s inside. Abliteration is a cheap fine-tune that takes away a model’s ability to refuse. You find the direction in the weights that carries “no” and subtract it. The model then answers things a safety-tuned version would turn down. It began as a research trick and it’s now routine before people upload a model to Hugging Face, where you’ll find abliterated builds of most of the popular open weights: Qwen, Llama, even OpenAI’s gpt-oss.
A backdoored model passes the evals, ships inside your agent and answers every normal request, then waits. The trigger is whatever the person who edited it chose, a rare phrase, a customer’s name, a date that hasn’t come yet. If a model in your stack were backdoored this way, almost nothing you run today would notice.

El verano es, informativamente hablando, una mala fecha. Muy mala. Como respuesta al calor, el hemisferio norte se sume en una larga somnolencia que, por otro lado, nos da una excusa perfecta para escapar de lo urgente y volver la mirada sobre temas importantes.
Por eso, son buenas fechas para recordar a los grandes y reivindicar sus logros y hazañas. Y si hay unos héroes, unos héroes genuinos e inmerecidamente olvidados, esos son los que lucharon contra la física, la química y el desaliento para crear el aire acondicionado. Va por ellos.
Ya los egipcios utilizaban sistemas para reducir el calor. Se usaban esteras o alfombras humedecidas para reducir la temperatura y la sequedad de las casas.
El primer ventilador giratorio parece ser chino en lo que suponemos que fue una evolución natural de su gusto por los abanicos. articles.summary:
This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration
The PRIMA system lets people with advanced AMD read and do crosswords. Here’s how it works.
More than 5 million people around the world with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) experience atrophy in their retinas. And until now, no treatment could restore their vision. The PRIMA system, which was approved in Europe in July and is awaiting FDA clearance in the US, changes that. It combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients who develop a blind spot in the middle of their vision due to advanced AMD. After training sessions, more than 80% of recipients were able to read, do crosswords, and use their phones.
Developed by the California-based Science Corporation, the system takes advantage of the fact that AMD doesn’t damage all retinal circuitry; only photoreceptors—the cells that convert light into an electrical signal—die off. PRIMA’s implant mimics those cells and transmits visual information directly to healthy eye circuitry and on to the brain. “We’re leveraging all of the body’s own natural functions to process and transmit the information,” says Frank Brodie, an ophthalmologist at the University of California, San Francisco, and Science Corp.'s chief medical officer for ophthalmology.

Candiru spyware was delivered to devices at Al Jazeera Media Network via targeted online advertisements in a zero-click attack that required only rendering the malicious ads on the victim's device.
Researchers at Citizen Labs investigating the attacks referred to this technique as AdFection, noting that their report is the first public technical confirmation of mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads.

El hallazgo. Durante una expedición de tres semanas, los investigadores recuperaron 48 flechas, una cantidad bastante elevada para lo que suele ser habitual. Las piezas pertenecieron a la Edad de Piedra y del Bronce, dos periodos muy antiguos para lo que estaban acostumbrados a encontrar.

articles.title: El error más famoso de Windows existe por una elección inesperada que casi nadie conoce

Pocas imágenes son tan reconocibles en la historia de la computación como la pantalla azul de la muerte, conocida popularmente como BSOD. Desde hace décadas, millones de usuarios de Windows se han topado con ella cuando el sistema operativo colapsa. Aunque muchos podrían pensar que el color azul fue una elección cuidadosa de Microsoft, la realidad es mucho más simple de lo que imaginas.
El origen del pantallazo de la muerte se remonta a los tiempos de Windows NT. De acuerdo con Dave Plummer, el antiguo ingeniero de Microsoft que programó el administrador de tareas, el color de esta pantalla está asociado a las herramientas de trabajo de su autor, John Vert.
Plummer explicó en un video de YouTube que Vert usaba un equipo MIPS RISC para desarrollo, cuyo firmware mostraba texto blanco sobre fondo azul. A esto se suma que la versión del editor de código SlickEdit que usaba en ese tiempo también tenía configurada por defecto esta combinación. El exingeniero de Microsoft añadió que en sus inicios, la pantalla azul de la muerte tenía otra connotación.
“Nunca escuché el término 'pantalla azul de la muerte' en Microsoft”, dijo Plummer. “Lo llamábamos principalmente pantalla azul, o más frecuentemente, comprobación de errores”. Esta se activaba cuando se producía un error que amenazaba con corromper el sistema, obligando al usuario a reiniciar su ordenador y perder todo en el proceso.

articles.title: Jev is Vercel's fastest-adopted AI model ever | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Jev has become the fastest adopted AI model ever — at least by some measures.
Vercel data published on Thursday shows that, within two weeks of its launch, the buzzy decision model was being used by 35% of paid teams, with nearly double the reach of the second most popular model, Sonnet 5.5. It’s the fastest adoption a model has ever seen in its first two weeks, according to Vercel’s data, and a major accomplishment for the model’s creators, TypeSafe AI.
Published in limited release on September 15, Jev is designed as a lightweight tool for choosing between a few predetermined outputs. Limiting the outputs lets the model run cheaper and faster than alternatives like Sonnet, making it ideal for classifying large quantities of data quickly. That new approach has attracted significant buzz in the weeks since Jev’s release — inspiring competing offerings from OpenAI and Amazon, among others — but until now there has been little hard data to back up the good vibes.
The data comes from Vercel’s AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter. It’s a necessarily limited view — particularly at risk of undercounting major labs like OpenAI and Anthropic that offer their own APIs — but it shows the buzz around Jev really did translate into actual usage. In fact, Vercel was an early adopter of Jev, using it to replace GPT-6 Luna for classifying harmful commands.

articles.title: How Paystack changed since Stripe bought it six years ago
articles.summary:
In October 2020, Stripe agreed to buy Paystack, a Lagos startup that helped businesses take payments online, for $200 million, the largest acquisition of a Nigerian startup. At the time, Paystack had 60,000 customers.
Stripe said the deal would fund new products and help pull Africa’s scattered payments market together and that Paystack would keep running on its own. Shola Akinlade, its chief executive, promised more countries, more payment channels and more services.
Six years after the acquisition, he has fulfilled that promise. In 2020, Paystack made money by taking a cut each time a business collected payment online, a model that needs scale. It charges 1.5% plus ₦100 per transaction, capped at ₦2,000, so a ₦10,000 order earns it ₦250, about 19 cents.
This model earns income only when money moves; unlike a bank that holds customers’ money, it can lend or invest it at a higher rate than it pays for it, and that income keeps coming for as long as the balances stay, with or without transactions.
Brazil’s Nubank shows how well this works. It ended 2025 with $41.9 billion in deposits, paid 87% of the interbank rate to fund itself, and made $2.9 billion. Worldwide, interest made up 46% of payments revenue in 2024, according to McKinsey.
Six years on, the company Stripe bought has changed shape. It now owns a microfinance bank and a consumer app. Its path shows why African fintechs keep becoming banks and how hard the last step is.

The DC council passed the Restricting Egregious Scalping Against Live Entertainment Amendment (RESALE) Act in June. Set to become law on January 1, 2027, it ensures that tickets purchased for shows can't be resold for more than 10% of the original price, including fees and taxes. It also limits the service fee that a resale marketplace can charge to 10% of that same original price. Tickets to most sporting events and movie tickets are exempt.
That sounds like a law that would be welcomed by everyone other than scalpers profiting from the tickets. But the resale sites themselves are also unhappy about it, unsurprisingly.
Four of these companies – SeatGeek, Vivid Seats, Gametime and TickPick – are so against the RESALE Act that they're suing to stop it from going into effect.
Brian Berry, Executive Director of the Ticket Policy Forum (TPF), a trade association of online ticket marketplaces, claims the law will simply drive ticket scams into shady, unregulated areas, subjecting fans to greater risks from street-side scams and increased fraud.

articles.title: Grafana Applies SLOs and Error Budgets to AI Agent Behaviour
articles.summary:
Grafana Labs is proposing a familiar reliability engineering approach for one of the less familiar problems in modern software: how to measure whether an AI agent is actually behaving well. In a recent article, the company describes using evaluations, service-level objectives (SLOs) and error budgets to turn behaviours such as hallucination, task fulfilment, toxicity, and cost into measurable targets that can be monitored over time.
The idea addresses a fundamental limitation of conventional application observability. Traditional metrics can tell engineers that an agent responded quickly, encountered no technical errors, and consumed a certain number of tokens, but none necessarily indicate whether its answer was correct, grounded in available information, or useful to the user. Grafana's approach is to evaluate the behaviour itself and turn the result into an SLI that can be measured against an SLO.
The first step is evaluation. An evaluation examines an agent interaction and determines whether it met a particular behavioural criterion. Grafana describes examples including whether a response was grounded in its supplied context, fulfilled the user's request, contained toxic content, exposed personal information, or succumbed to prompt injection. Evaluations can use another language model as a judge, but deterministic checks such as regular expressions can also be used where the behaviour can be identified without an LLM.

articles.title: Israeli Ad Firm Doubled as Candiru’s Zero-Click Spyware Delivery Channel
articles.summary:
Candiru spyware has infected devices at international news network Al Jazeera in zero-click attacks, via targeted advertisements, Canadian internet watchdog group Citizen Lab reports.
As part of the operation, dubbed AdFection, ads purchased by Israeli company Discover-Tech were used to de-anonymize, fingerprint, and infect users, and also allow threat actors to track millions of devices.
As part of the online advertising ecosystem, companies bid at billions of daily Real-Time Bidding (RTB) auctions hosted on ad exchanges for a chance to serve an ad to a user.
Ad exchanges collect extensive device and user data that enables tracking, and ads may contain code that runs in the user’s application or browser, typically for tracking users, impressions, and clicks.
However, ads may also contain malicious code potentially leading to malware infections and, courtesy of the various identifiers used within the ecosystem, could be used to target specific individuals with spyware, Citizen Lab says.
Discover-Tech, a seemingly legitimate advertising company, is likely the front for a large campaign involving spyware infection and espionage, serving as a bridge between ad vendors and mercenary spyware vendors.
Its Controlium platform enables the de-anonymization of millions of users, device fingerprinting, and zero-click hacking when an ad is displayed on the victim’s device.

articles.title: Understanding The Zero Trust Definition and Its Role in Modern Cybersecurity - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A contractor signs in from a managed laptop, an employee opens a finance application from home, and a service account calls an API from the cloud. While all three requests may look legitimate, any one of them could also become an attacker’s route into sensitive systems.
That tension sits behind the zero trust definition. Zero trust treats identity, device condition, resource sensitivity, and surrounding context as evidence to check, rather than assuming that a connection to a corporate network makes an access request safe. For security leaders, this shift is less about buying another control and more about changing how access decisions are made across a fragmented enterprise.
What Does Zero Trust Mean for an Enterprise?
The basic idea of zero trust is often compressed into “never trust, always verify”. While it is a useful brief, it’s not quite enough.
A practical zero trust definition has three parts:
- Access is granted explicitly
- Permissions are kept as narrow as the task permits
- Security teams work on the assumption that an account, endpoint, or workload may already be compromised
And the resulting decision should be specific to that user, device, application, and moment.
Now, readers who need a fuller explanation of the underlying model can refer to this complete zero trust definition guide.

In many regards, vibe-coded apps are the new shadow IT, with employees deploying software beyond the oversight of their IT teams.
And that’s why Cloudflare wants to bring some order to proceedings. On Thursday, the company announced the release of Void, a collection of three open-source tools that includes a self-hosted platform where companies can deploy and manage their employees’ AI-built applications. D-Link, Ubiquiti devices hijacked by hackers to plunder stolen bandwidth
Someone hacked network-attached devices to install... legitimate software?
- Attackers exploited vulnerable devices to install legitimate bandwidth-sharing software and hijack internet connections
- Compromised systems were covertly added to proxy networks, enabling anonymous criminal activity
- Campaign affected at least 143 devices across 34 countries, highlighting patching and access-control failures
When threat actors break into a system, they don’t need to install malware to make use of the compromised endpoint - they can install perfectly legal, normal software, and still walk away with a paycheck they didn’t earn.
A recent proxyjacking campaign spotted by security researchers GreyNoise impacted hundreds of devices in dozens of countries.
Proxyjacking
Proxyjacking is a type of attack in which a device is hijacked and assimilated into a proxy network. Usually, cybercriminals would break into a computer, install malware and create a proxy network of their own, which they can later rent or use themselves. Threat actors are always in need of “clean” and unflagged devices and IP addresses behind which they can hide, making residential proxies - both malicious and legal - highly wanted services.

Luu opened the session by noting three core drivers: AI fails differently from traditional software by generating convincing inaccuracies rather than crashing; coding agents are generating production code faster than humans can review; and sensitive data has new places to leak through prompts, context windows, and retrieved documents.
Xiong, Head of AI Ops for Managed Services at ThoughtWorks, highlighted the widespread issue of "semantic drift" in LLM pipelines. articles.title: Experiment shows liquid metal TIM doesn’t dry out; it turns solid — two-year electron microscope test finds gallium bonds with copper coolers, and nickel plating keeps the layer about 10 times thinner
articles.summary:
Experiment shows liquid metal TIM doesn’t dry out; it turns solid — two-year electron microscope test finds gallium bonds with copper coolers, and nickel plating keeps the layer about 10 times thinner
Liquid metal’s hardened layer conducts heat about a quarter as well as the copper it replaces.
YouTuber hardware enthusiast and Thermal Grizzly boss der8auer tested a two-year-old liquid metal thermal interface material (TIM) application with an electron microscope in his new video, discovering that it doesn’t dry out. Instead, the gallium bonds with the copper in a reaction to form a solid compound. On copper, that layer’s heat conduction performance is about one-quarter of the bare metal’s, and nickel plating keeps it about 10 times thinner.
His test showed the TIM as liquid after one hour, no liquid visible with crystals everywhere at the two-month mark, and then unchanged after two years. “After a total of two years, this honestly did not change further,” he said. The test relied on storing the setup in a vacuum or a nitrogen-filled box between sessions to avoid oxidation.
The TIM in question is an alloy of gallium and indium, often including tin, which is liquid at room temperature (Thermal Grizzly sells its own as Conductonaut); gallium melts at about 30 degrees Celsius, with the gallium-indium-tin mix melting at only 11 degrees. articles.title: Why an Ethiopian nurse built Medanit
articles.summary:
In a hospital emergency ward, a three-hour delay searching for prescribed medication is not an inconvenience—it can be fatal. In 2020, while working in an Ethiopian public emergency room, nurse and social worker Beamlak Alemayehu watched patients lose critical hours moving from pharmacy to pharmacy just to locate essential drugs and tests. Some never survived the wait. Determined to fix the fragmentation, she set out to build Medanit in 2022 as a clean digital directory. But when she approached clinics and pharmacies, she hit a wall: between 80% and 90% of them still ran entirely on manual paper ledgers. There were simply no digital records to plug into. Realising she could not just be a consumer-facing middleman, Alemayehu took on the heavy lifting: writing hospital management software, building electronic medical records (EMR), setting up pharmacy delivery logistics, and launching a dedicated call centre to ensure rural farmers and mothers without smartphones were not left behind. Today, Medanit has onboarded over 520 doctors, logged 1.2 million platform visitors, and secured backing from the Bayer Foundation as it prepares to expand into Rwanda and Zambia. In this feature, JOHN ADOYI tells the story of an Ethiopian nurse who stopped waiting for healthcare infrastructure to arrive—and built it herself.

articles.title: Uber Automates Dependency Analysis Across Its Service Mesh
articles.summary:
Uber has developed an automated approach to mapping service dependencies and classifying how downstream failures propagate across its service mesh. The system uses RPC middleware to correlate caller and callee failures across production requests, classifying dependencies as fail-close, fail-open, or unknown. Uber says the approach has cataloged dependencies for critical APIs and indexed most fail-close anomalies across its service mesh.
The Uber Engineering team highlighted the motivation in a LinkedIn post,
When a request fails, how do you figure out what actually caused it? At Uber’s scale, that gets complicated fast. With thousands of services and dependencies interacting, traditional tracing can’t always give engineers the full picture quickly enough.
In a microservices architecture, requests can traverse deeply nested and asynchronous service calls, making it difficult to determine which dependency contributed to a failure. Uber defines a fail-close dependency as one whose failure can consistently cause its caller to fail. A fail-open dependency can fail without causing its caller to fail, while insufficient evidence results in an unknown classification. The classification can then be applied across call paths to identify how failures may propagate toward an originating API.
Uber initially considered distributed tracing for establishing these relationships, but found sampling too slow for rare failures. The company says more than 99.9% of requests complete without errors…

Si l’on n’entend plus parler de Blue Origin et SpaceX, Rocket Lab s’impose aussi comme un sérieux acteur dans le domaine des fusées. Son petit lanceur, Electron, reste sur 56 succès consécutifs. Mais désormais, l’entreprise est attendue au tournant avec Neutron, qui sera en mesure de transporter 13 tonnes en orbite basse.
Dotée d’un premier étage réutilisable, sa coiffe originale s’ouvre comme une mâchoire d’hippopotame pour libérer le second étage, avant de se refermer pour retourner sur Terre. Problème, son calendrier ne cesse de glisser : annoncée en 2021 pour un premier vol en 2024, celui-ci a été repoussé à 2025, puis 2026.
Pas de vol avant 2027
Mais ce mercredi 14 octobre, Peter Beck, P.-D.G de la firme, a annoncé que Neutron volerait en 2027 au plus tôt. Car en janvier, un réservoir a éclaté lors d’un test de pression. Celui-ci avait été fabriqué à la main par un sous-traitant, en attendant que la machine automatisée de dépose de fibres de carbone soit opérationnelle.
Rocket Lab a donc renforcé la structure en épaississant certaines zones. Mais ces parties ont à leur tour posé problème : lors de la fabrication d’un dôme, le couvercle bombé d’un réservoir, des poches d’air se sont formées entre les couches de carbone.

articles.title: Cette seconde spéciale, qu'on ajoute pour s'adapter aux caprices de la rotation terrestre, pourrait bientôt disparaître
articles.summary:
Tous les quatre ans, février gagne un jour à la faveur d’une année bissextile. La raison est astronomique : la Terre met environ 365 jours un quart à faire le tour du Soleil. Ajouter un 29 février tous les quatre ans compense le décalage. Sans cet ajustement, les équinoxes et les solstices glisseraient de plus en plus tard dans le calendrier, entraînant avec eux le jour marquant le début de chaque saisons.
Car pendant des millénaires, le jour a été défini comme la durée d’une rotation complète de la Terre sur elle-même. Mais cette rotation n’est pas toujours parfaitement régulière. Pour gagner en précision, les systèmes modernes de mesure du temps ont cessé de s’appuyer sur elle.
Ce changement a créé un décalage entre l’ancienne définition de la seconde et celle utilisée aujourd’hui. En effet, au fil des années, les systèmes modernes de mesure du temps peuvent se décaler de quelques secondes par rapport au mouvement de la Terre. Pour corriger cet écart, les spécialistes de la mesure du temps ont recours à ce qu’on appelle une « seconde intercalaire ». De la même manière que les années bissextiles maintiennent nos calendriers en phase avec la révolution de la Terre autour du Soleil, les secondes intercalaires maintiennent nos horloges en phase avec sa rotation quotidienne.
Mais en octobre 2026, l’organisation internationale chargée de la mesure du temps pourrait revoir les règles d’ajout des secondes intercalaires.

Whalefall (2026) podría tener una de las premisas más insólitas del año. En especial, porque la historia de un buzo que es tragado por una ballena y debe escapar del interior del animal es disparatada por necesidad. No obstante, la dirección de Brian Duffield convierte esa historia en aparente sin sentido, en un brillante ejercicio de acción. Más interesante todavía, en una reflexión madura, profunda y emotiva, sobre la supervivencia y el sufrimiento emocional. Todo mientras, sí, nuestro esforzado protagonista Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams, de Resident Evil) intenta salir de las entrañas de un cetáceo descomunal.
Por lo que gran parte del mérito de Whalefall es convertir un relato con apenas personas en pantallas, en una reflexión de la naturaleza humana. Más allá, en utilizar todos los tropos de las survival movies para subvertirlos con habilidad y un asombroso vigor. El resultado es una cinta que no solo no aburre jamás, aunque prácticamente estamos viendo el mismo encuadre todo el tiempo. Además, es lo suficientemente inteligente para combinar en una misma trama la idea del duelo y el motivo por el cual el dolor puede impulsar a vivir. Ambos puntos de vista extremos sobre sobrevivir a una tragedia que Whalefall analiza con buen gusto y sin caer en sensiblerías.

articles.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Elorian, the Palo Alto AI startup that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before it launched a product, released its first model on Friday, TechCrunch has exclusively learned.
The model, Glimpse, is launching as a research preview with API access and a chat interface. The thesis? Today’s AI models, for all their skill with language and code, still can’t really see.
Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens, and then reason about it in text — like describing a photo from memory. Glimpse keeps going back to the source. Mid-reasoning, it can crop into a region, pull specific frames from a video, or run code to measure or compare what it’s looking at, a mechanism Elorian calls a “visual scratch space.” Think of someone pinching to zoom on a phone photo to double-check what they thought they saw.
For former Google DeepMind researcher and Elorian CEO Andrew Dai, one of the clearest signs that AI still couldn’t really see came on game night.
Last year he photographed a board game he’d just finished with friends and asked a frontier model who was winning. It couldn’t say. Board games “each have their own visual language, each have their own iconography, symbols,” he told TechCrunch. “To an adult, it’s quite easy to understand what’s going on with minimal text, but these models aren’t able to intuit what the symbols mean.”
“Humans can look at Ikea diagrams, with no text, and assemble Ikea furniture, right? Why can’t AI models?” he said…

On prediction markets, trading volume—the total value of contracts bought and sold—typically tracks roughly with the odds of a given outcome; frontrunners attract far more volume than long shots. articles.title: Zod Brings In-Process Schema Compilation and a 9x Cut in Memory Footprint
articles.summary:
Zod, the TypeScript-first schema validation library created by Colin McDonnell, released Zod 4.5 on August 28, 2026, introducing schema compilation, an order-of-magnitude cut in schema memory usage, and a batch of long-requested helpers. Zod 4.6 followed on September 9, extending that work and fixing a recursive-schema memory regression. The major compilation and memory-footprint changes arrived in 4.5, which remains the focus here, but developers upgrading now should also account for the subsequent release.
The flagship addition is z.compile(), which turns any schema into a precompiled validator that parses the same data three to nine times faster. The compiled schema behaves exactly like the original, with no special rules. Importantly, as McDonnell explains, compilation happens in-process rather than at build time, so there is no bundler plugin or codegen step to wire up.
Teams that want this applied everywhere can add import "zod/compile" at the top of an entry point, or run node --import zod/compile app.js, after which every schema is compiled lazily the first time it parses data.
By memoising bound methods instead of allocating them per instance, a bare z.string() now retains 784 bytes of heap rather than 7.5kb, a roughly nine-fold reduction. safeParse() also skips stack-trace capture on failure, making invalid input about 7.5 times cheaper to reject. articles.title: AI agents vs. Kubernetes: where each belongs in the control loop

AI agents vs. Kubernetes: where each belongs in the control loop
Kubernetes has always relied on agents, just not the kind dominating today’s AI conversations. A controller watches the current state, compares it with a declared desired state, and takes action to close the gap. That resemblance makes AI agents and Kubernetes operators sound interchangeable. They are not.
This question is no longer theoretical. Over the past 18 months, agent tooling has moved from a side project to part of the cloud-native stack. CNCF has accepted agent frameworks into its Sandbox, and Kubernetes SIG Apps has taken on Agent Sandbox as a subproject for running agent workloads safely.
Platform teams are already deciding what an agent can change in a live cluster, usually one pull request at a time and without a written policy. By default, the boundary between reasoning and execution is set by convention rather than design.

An AI agent is useful when the desired outcome is clear but the path isn’t. It can investigate an unfamiliar situation, gather context from several systems, weigh tradeoffs, and propose a course of action.

articles.title: The Future of Malware Protection in an Increasingly Connected World - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A compromised laptop once gave security teams a reasonably clear place to start. Now the same infection may touch a cloud workload, reuse an employee’s session token, probe an operational technology network, and call home through encrypted traffic before the first alert reaches the SOC.
That expanding chain of dependencies is changing malware protection. Organizations still need to block malicious files, but the harder task is recognizing hostile behavior across devices, identities, applications, and networks that weren’t designed to share security context. For CISOs, this is becoming less of a product question and more of an architectural one.
Why Traditional Malware Defenses Are Losing Context
Signature-based detection hasn’t become irrelevant because known malware should be stopped quickly and cheaply, without consuming analyst time.
The current problem is, however, what happens around the file. Attackers now can use legitimate administrative tools, stolen credentials, malicious scripts, and trusted cloud services to advance an intrusion. In other cases, they’ll change a payload just enough to avoid a known signature.
Australia’s Cyber Security Centre has also warned that crypters are being used to disguise malware and make it harder for antivirus software to detect.
Security teams therefore need to view malware protection for businesses as a connected set of controls, not a scanner installed on every endpoint. Detection must follow activity across the entire attack path, …

articles.title: Google EnvHarness Enables Self-Evolving Agents to Learn in Dynamics Environments
articles.summary:
Google researchers open-sourced EnvHarness, a framework that dynamically adapts agent-training environments to an agent's weaknesses without modifying the agent, environment, or evaluation system. The researchers say this approach can improve both learning effectiveness and efficiency while helping agents overcome their weaknesses.
According to the research authors, self-evolving agents typically improve by rewriting their prompts and acquiring new skills, but rarely adapt the environments in which they operate. This has important consequences:
An agent that keeps improving against a frozen benchmark eventually stops learning from it. The start states, the rules and the feedback are the same for every learner at every stage, so once the agent can solve the tasks, the environment has nothing further to teach.
Environment generation, the researchers explain, is expensive, requiring domain-specific pipelines and often relying on expensive or unreliable verifiers. Despite these efforts, the resulting environments remain static. To make it easier for engineers to train agents in adaptive environments, they created EnvHarness.
EnvHarness acts as a programmable layer of plug-in components that wraps a static environment, changing only the interface the agent interacts through. By dynamically introducing mutations, it can reshape the environment's behavior without altering its underlying structure or evaluation system.

He’d bought the Plustek OpticFilm 8200i because it was listed as supported, then discovered that the manufacturer had swapped in a chipset no Linux driver recognized. He tried getting Claude Code to produce a working driver and got nowhere for a long time, so he eventually set the project aside for a few months.
When he returned to the project, Schaller tried a different approach. Within hours, he had his first recognizable scan. A few days later, the driver supported infrared scanning, too.
Schaller has since released the underlying approach as an open-source project called hw-harness under an MIT license. Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era,” with the basic building blocks like actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards still being rebuilt.
This view runs counter to those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have its “ChatGPT moment” — that day when the shockingly capable chatbot was launched in late 2022. (General Intuition CEO Pim de Witte told Equity earlier this year that a single general foundation model would make much of today’s specialized robotics work redundant, and be that moment.)
On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Dominic-Madori Davis caught up with Vishwanath to discuss where she’s writing first checks as the founder and managing partner of Techable VC. They also talked about what she’s learned as one of the first women executives to spin out of Nvidia and launch her own early-stage firm investing in physical AI across robotics, materials science, and life sciences.

articles.title: AI has lowered the barrier to building. Here's what that means for engineers.
articles.summary:
AI has lowered the barrier to building. Here’s what that means for engineers.
For most of software’s history, building meant writing code. Not just understanding it, but producing it. The entry point was steep by design: fluency in at least one language, working knowledge of system architecture, enough production scar tissue to know what questions to ask before writing the first line. The barrier was real, and both sides of it understood why it existed.
AI coding tools, natural language interfaces, and agentic workflows have started shifting what it takes to go from an idea to working software. A product manager can now prototype a functional application without writing a single line of code. A data engineer can spin up a pipeline in hours that would have taken a team a week to scope and test. Domain expertise that used to be locked inside someone’s head is becoming portable in a way it never was before.
“The constraint wasn’t the knowledge. It was the translation layer between knowing something and being able to build something. AI is removing that layer.”

articles.summary:
Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) is an open-source project with over 200K GitHub stars that connects coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to reverse-engineering tools like Ghidra, Hopper, and IDA. The project lets developers inspect compiled binaries, trace function calls, and investigate how applications implement specific features.
REA uses MCP servers to expose reverse-engineering tools to agents, which can query disassemblers, inspect functions and cross-references, trace program behavior, and iteratively test hypotheses against the binary. The tool also supports static analysis of JavaScript and Electron applications and .NET assemblies, using the results to guide further investigation. REA runs locally and does not claim to recover the original source code.
Source: REA project on GitHub
The showcases on GitHub demonstrate how REA can trace Notion’s Electron clipboard implementation, reconstruct a sound-panning function from the classic game DX-Ball with tests matching all 3205 original x86 cases and all 63 compiled function bytes, and recover bullet-ring angle calculations from the 16-bit code of the DOS game Touhou 4.
On Hacker News, some practitioners question what the project adds beyond asking an AI coding agent to install and use Ghidra, an open source tool developed by the NSA to analyze compiled programs. articles.title: Así es la rutina ideal para manejar el estrés desde la mañana, sin meditaciones ni mindfulness
articles.summary:
La resiliencia y la flexibilidad psicológica son dos cualidades esenciales para nuestra salud mental, a las que a menudo no prestamos la atención que merecen. Solemos centrarnos en cómo enfrentarnos a las consecuencias del estrés o incluso cómo prevenirlo, pero pasamos de largo sobre el hecho de que a veces, aunque estresarnos sea inevitable, podemos prevenir sus peores consecuencias. Esto, básicamente, es lo que consiguen las personas con buena resiliencia y flexibilidad psicológica. Es algo que puede entrenarse a base de terapia. Sin embargo, también son cualidades que pueden alcanzarse modificando ciertos hábitos de nuestro día a día.
Sueño, alimentación y ejercicio. Un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Binghamton ha encuestado a 400 estudiantes para comparar sus hábitos con sus niveles de resiliencia y flexibilidad psicológica. Así, han observado que hay una serie de hábitos muy concretos que abundan en los jóvenes que se enfrentan de una forma más positiva al estrés.
Para empezar, el hecho de no saltarse los desayunos marca una gran diferencia. En general, en las encuestas los resultados empezaban a verse en los participantes que desayunaban al menos cinco veces a la semana. articles.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.”
The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.”
This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal.
At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers. CERT-In described no such hacking in India, where the agents appear to have simply used the access left lying around.

Artificial intelligence is changing how software is designed, built, and delivered. What once required specialized research teams and significant computing resources is increasingly accessible through APIs that connect applications to powerful AI models.
Developers can now integrate conversational assistants, image generation, video creation, and other intelligent capabilities into products without building every underlying system from scratch.
Yet this progress has introduced a new challenge. As the AI ecosystem expands, developers must navigate an increasingly diverse landscape of models, providers, interfaces, and technical requirements. Choosing a capable model is no longer the only consideration. Teams must also decide how to integrate it, maintain the connection, manage costs, handle failures, and adapt when a better alternative becomes available.
This is where the idea of a unified AI API becomes important. Rather than treating every model as a separate integration project, developers can adopt a more consistent approach to accessing AI capabilities. Such an approach can simplify development, support experimentation, and make applications more adaptable as the technology continues to evolve.

Acto seguido, no ha dudado en arremeter contra los conductores a los que les pilla un radar. Un radar fijo, se entiende, porque el máximo responsable de Tráfico ha dejado muchas cosas en el tintero.
"Por tonto". Las palabras son de Pere Navarro y han sido pronunciadas a El Comercio con motivo de una entrevista aprovechando su presencia en la Convención Nacional de Directivos de la Dirección General de Tráfico (DGT) que se está llevando a cabo en Asturias.
Allí, preguntado por este medio sobre los radares, Navarro ha asegurado:
"Lo mínimo que puede hacer el conductor es frenar, pasar el radar y luego hacer lo que quiera. Pero si ni siquiera hace esto... A veces decimos que la sanción no es tanto por exceso de velocidad como por tonto. Si te ponen un gran cartel que te dice que hay un radar, ¿para qué continúas con el exceso de velocidad?"
"Lo llevamos con resignación". Así describe el director de la DGT qué siente cuando alguien dice que todo lo que hace el organismo está pensado para recaudar. "La velocidad o causa accidentes o los agrava. Y para hacer frente a la velocidad, aquí y en cualquier país del mundo, están los radares", se defiende.
